title: Cup product with closed supports
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\Lambda$ be a commutative torsion ring, and work on the small etale sites, with constant coefficient sheaves $\Lambda_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and module derived categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], put $V=Z\times_XW$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and write $h:V\hookrightarrow X$ for their scheme-theoretic intersection. Thus $Z\cap W$ in the support notation below means this closed support. Let $F,G\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, let $a,b\in\mathbf Z$, and let $\alpha\in H_Z^a(X,F)$ and $\beta\in H_W^b(X,G)$, with the supported groups of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Use [lem-pur-supported-hom] to regard these classes as morphisms $\alpha:i_*\Lambda_Z\to F[a]$ and $\beta:j_*\Lambda_W\to G[b]$.

For an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, $K\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the supported group in this construction means
$$
 H_V^r(X,K):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)}(h_*\Lambda_V,K[r]).
$$
This extends the bounded-below supported groups by [lem-pur-supported-hom]; the unbounded closed-support interpretation is also the derived-Hom description of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]. Thus the output below remains meaningful when $F\otimes^L_\Lambda G$ is not bounded below.

Here is the specified coefficient identification used in the definition. For an etale $U\to X$, restrict a section of $\Lambda_Z$ on $Z\times_XU$ and a section of $\Lambda_W$ on $W\times_XU$ to $V\times_XU$, and multiply them. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and sheaf tensor universal property [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] give a map
$$
 \mu:i_*\Lambda_Z\otimes_{\Lambda_X}j_*\Lambda_W\longrightarrow h_*\Lambda_V.
$$
This is an isomorphism: closed immersions are finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so their stalks are $\Lambda$ on the support and $0$ elsewhere by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]. The tensor over the constant ring $\Lambda$ in [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] agrees after sheafification with the tensor over $\Lambda_X$: a section of $\Lambda_X$ is locally represented by an element of the constant presheaf, so the $\Lambda_X$-balancing relation is locally already a $\Lambda$-balancing relation. The preceding stalk identifications respect scalar multiplication, since their maps commute with multiplication by every element of $\Lambda$. Hence, by that tensor-stalk lemma, the stalk of $\mu$ is multiplication $\Lambda\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda\to\Lambda$ on the intersection and the isomorphism between zero modules off it; [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] proves the claim. These coefficient sheaves are flat in the sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]: tensoring an exact sequence and taking stalks gives tensor with either $\Lambda$ or $0$, which preserves exactness, and [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] together with stalk conservativity detects that exactness. Their degree-zero complexes are K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1), so $\mu$ induces the canonical isomorphism
$$
 \theta:i_*\Lambda_Z\otimes^L_\Lambda j_*\Lambda_W\xrightarrow{\sim}h_*\Lambda_V.
$$
Derived tensor here is [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the shift identification $F[a]\otimes^L_\Lambda G[b]\cong(F\otimes^L_\Lambda G)[a+b]$ is the canonical one supplied by its exactness in each variable [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated].

The supported cup product $\alpha\smile\beta$ is, by definition, the following composite, read in $H_{Z\cap W}^{a+b}(X,F\otimes^L_\Lambda G)$:
$$
 h_*\Lambda_V\xrightarrow{\theta^{-1}}
 i_*\Lambda_Z\otimes^L_\Lambda j_*\Lambda_W
 \xrightarrow{\alpha\otimes^L\beta}
 F[a]\otimes^L_\Lambda G[b]
 \xrightarrow{\sim}(F\otimes^L_\Lambda G)[a+b].
$$

split_report.summary: Made all objects and the etale coefficient category explicit; replaced the mismatched pro-etale-only tensor definition with the existing etale derived-tensor node. Defined the coefficient map by restriction and multiplication, verified its isomorphism and flatness using existing finite-stalk, tensor-stalk and exactness statements, and displayed the shift map separately. Repaired the boundedness gap by specifying the unbounded supported-Hom target convention, agreeing with the existing bounded-below groups. No new nodes; all ingredients already exist. The report records STATEMENT-DISPUTED, the Tor counterexample and the explicit topology clarification. Searches are recorded exactly as run, with invalid queries and an invalid directory distinguished from genuine negative results.
